notes: REQ inventory note: only register-schemas/spec.md uses the canonical capability-dir layout. The other 8 specs live as flat .md files at openspec/specs/*.md and use '### Requirement: <Name> [<tier>]' headings without IDs in the canonical [A-Z]{2,4}-[0-9]+ format. The scanner synthesised stable REQ slugs from the heading names (e.g. 'REQ-Project-Lifecycle'). /opsx-annotate will need to either (a) tolerate slug-style IDs, or (b) the architecture should retrofit canonical IDs first.

Reverse pass: removed-lines cache is only 163 lines — planix has almost no git history (cache built in 0.5s). All unimplemented REQs collapsed to Bucket 3b: no meaningful keyword matches for kanban/tasks/timeEntry/procest/myWork (one false-positive hit on the word 'Kanban' came from the 'Board view coming soon' placeholder string). Treat 3b list as 'planned, never started' rather than 'removed'.

REQ-Version-based-skip-logic is annotated as NEEDS-REVIEW: SettingsService::loadConfiguration takes a $force flag and propagates it, but BOTH callers (InitializeSettings::run and SettingsController::load) pass force=true unconditionally. The version-skip behaviour exists only inside OpenRegister's ConfigurationService — the planix-side never exercises the skip path. Either the REQ is satisfied by delegation, or it is effectively dead code on the planix side.

REQ-Project-List-UI was assigned to DashboardController::page/catchAll with confidence 0.70 NEEDS-REVIEW: these are the SPA entry points that load every Vue route including ProjectList. The mapping is correct but coarse — the REQ is really implemented by the Vue components.

REQ-OpenRegister-Gate sits in projects.md but is implemented in App.vue and SettingsService::isOpenRegisterAvailable. Kept the capability mapping but the REQ may belong in a shared 'app-shell' capability if more apps adopt the same gate pattern.

REQ-Loading-and-Error-States in projects.md classified as 3b deliberately: the projects store and Vue views DO show loading spinners and error states, but there is no single method that 'implements' it — it's a cross-cutting concern. /opsx-annotate would need to tag many methods; flagging as 3b lets a human decide whether to retire the REQ or split it.

REQ-i18n-Coverage in projects.md classified as 3b: every user-facing string in src/ uses t('planix', ...) so the REQ is effectively satisfied, but again there is no specific method to annotate. Consider retiring this REQ in favour of an ADR-007 conformance gate.

Bucket 2a 'register-schemas' entry for lib/Settings/planix_register.json is informational only — the scanner enumerates .php and .vue/.js/.ts files, not JSON. The JSON file is the canonical implementation of REQ-All-5-schemas-defined and should be referenced when the human writes the ghost-change tasks.md.

ADR-001 direct-SQL finding on SettingsService::ensureRegisterPublicAccess is a real architectural smell — it reaches into the openregister_registers table directly with a raw UPDATE. Flagged for the human; not auto-fixed.
